definition: Machine learning with a fixed, driven dynamical system (the reservoir) whose states feed a trained linear readout; only the readout is learned.
The fixed dynamical system in reservoir computing: driven by the input, never trained, read out through a set of features.
The trained part of a reservoir computer: usually a linear map from the reservoir features to the output, fitted by ridge regression.
A random recurrent network of tanh units driven by the input, with only a linear readout trained (Jaeger 2001).
The spiking-neuron form of reservoir computing (Maass, Natschläger and Markram 2002).
The largest absolute value of a matrix's eigenvalues; in an echo state network it sets how slowly perturbations of the state decay.
The size of a reservoir's input weights, which sets how far the input drives the units into their nonlinearity.
The factor a in a leaky-integrator reservoir unit, x ← (1−a)x + a·f(·); its inverse is the unit's time constant in steps.
The first steps of a reservoir run, discarded because the state still depends on the arbitrary initial condition.
Feeding the true past target, instead of the model's own output, back into a recurrent model during training.
Reservoir computing without a reservoir: delayed inputs and their low-order monomials used directly as the features of a linear readout (Gauthier et al. 2021).
The property that a driven reservoir's state, after a washout, depends only on the input history and not on its initial state.
The property of a filter whose output depends less and less on inputs further in the past (Boyd and Chua 1985).
The state of a driven system becoming a fixed function of the drive signal, so copies started apart converge.
An expansion of a nonlinear filter as a sum of multilinear terms in past inputs; it approximates every fading-memory filter.
The sum over delays d ≥ 1 of the squared correlation between a linear readout's best estimate of u(k−d) and u(k−d); at most the number of features for i.i.d. input.
The squared correlation r²(d) of the best linear reconstruction of the input d steps back, as a function of d.
The summed capacity of a reservoir to reconstruct an orthogonal basis of functions of its past inputs; at most the number of independent state variables (Dambre et al. 2012).
The fixed capacity budget of a reservoir: capacity spent on nonlinear functions of the input is taken from linear memory, and vice versa.
Reservoir computing in which the reservoir is a physical system (light, water, spins, mechanics) and only the readout is digital.
One of the time slots into which a single physical node's response is divided between inputs, each read as a separate feature.
Making one physical node act as many reservoir nodes by sampling it at several times per input.
A fixed sequence of weights multiplying the held input in a delay reservoir, one per virtual node.
Nonlinear autoregressive moving-average benchmark tasks whose target needs memory of n steps and products of inputs and outputs.
A delay differential equation, chaotic for delay 17 in its standard parameters, used as a forecasting benchmark.
Mean squared prediction error divided by the variance of the target; 1 is what predicting the mean achieves.
Predicting the XOR of the last n random bits; in ±1 coding a degree-n product that tests nonlinear memory.
The disturbance a measurement causes to the measured system; for a quantum reservoir, projective readout collapses the state and erases the coherences that carried input memory.
The statistical error of estimating an expectation value from $S$ single-shot outcomes, with standard deviation $\sqrt{(1-x^2)/S}$ for a $\pm1$ observable of mean $x$.
One execution of a quantum circuit or experiment ending in a measurement that returns a single outcome, such as one bitstring.
Hardware QRC readout in which the input sequence is replayed from a fresh state for each output time and measured at the end, giving undisturbed features at a cost of $S\,T$ runs.
A restart protocol that replays only the last $w$ inputs before each output, valid when the reservoir's memory fades within $w$ steps; it costs $S\,T\,w$ evolution steps instead of $S\,T(T+1)/2$.
A hardware QRC protocol that measures during a single pass through the input sequence, so the number of runs equals the number of shots rather than shots times sequence length.

A measurement that extracts little information per outcome and disturbs the state correspondingly little; a Gaussian pointer of width $\sigma$ dephases a qubit by $e^{-1/(2\sigma^2)}$ and adds variance $\sigma^2$ per outcome.
A model of measurement in which the observable shifts a continuous pointer whose readout has Gaussian spread $\sigma$; the spread sets the measurement strength.
Measuring some qubits partway through a circuit while the others continue coherently, usually followed by reset; the basis of online QRC on gate-based hardware.
Reading a collective signal from many identical copies of a system at once, as in NMR, which returns an expectation value in one run with little disturbance per copy.
Approximating evolution under $H = A + B$ by alternating short evolutions under $A$ and $B$; for a reservoir circuit its accuracy matters less than the mixing the circuit provides.
Using the intrinsic noise of a quantum processor as the dissipation that gives a reservoir fading memory, rather than treating it only as an error.
Neutral atoms held in optical tweezers and excited to Rydberg states, whose strong $1/r^6$ interactions realise Ising-type Hamiltonians and give full bitstring snapshots per shot.
A randomised-measurement method that estimates many low-weight observables from the same snapshots, with sample cost growing as $3^k\log M/\epsilon^2$ for $M$ Pauli observables of weight $k$.
The total number of measurement shots available for a task, which with the protocol and device timings fixes what reservoir size and feature set are usable.
Reservoir computing in which the fixed dynamical system is quantum: an input-driven quantum channel updates a state each step and only a linear readout of measured expectation values is trained.
The fixed, input-driven quantum system of a quantum reservoir computer, whose state carries a fading nonlinear memory of past inputs.
A driven system whose state obeys $r_k = A(s_k) r_{k-1} + b(s_k)$: linear in the state, nonlinear in the input; every quantum reservoir is one in the Pauli (Bloch) coordinates.
The real matrix of a quantum channel acting on the Pauli-basis coordinates $\operatorname{Tr}(P_\mu \rho)$ of a state.

The first quantum reservoir (2017): qubits with random XX couplings and a Z field, input written by resetting one qubit to $\sqrt{1-s}\vert0\rangle+\sqrt{s}\vert1\rangle$, read out through $\langle Z_i\rangle$ at virtual-node times.
Conservation of $Z_1Z_2\cdots Z_n$ by Hamiltonians built from $X_iX_j$ and $Z_i$ terms, which splits the dynamics into even and odd sectors.
Writing an input by discarding a qubit and re-preparing it in an input-dependent state; it encodes the input and supplies the dissipation that makes memory fade.
Injecting $\sqrt{1-s}\vert0\rangle+\sqrt{s}\vert1\rangle$, so the probability of measuring 1 equals the input $s$.
Encoding an input as a rotation angle, for example $R_y(\pi s)\vert0\rangle$.
Encoding an input in the relative phase of a superposition, for example $R_z(\pi s)\vert+\rangle$; invisible to Z readouts of a parity-symmetric reservoir at first order.
Encoding an input in a Hamiltonian or gate parameter; unitary on its own, so it needs separate dissipation for fading memory.
Reading a reservoir at several times between inputs (virtual nodes) to multiply the number of features.
Driving several independent small reservoirs with the same input and concatenating their features.
A product of Pauli Z operators on a subset of qubits; all $2^n-1$ of them can be estimated from the same computational-basis shots.
The expectation $\langle Z_iZ_j\rangle$ of two qubits, a cheap extra reservoir feature from the same bitstrings as $\langle Z_i\rangle$.
The ratio $\min(g_k,g_{k+1})/\max(g_k,g_{k+1})$ of consecutive energy gaps; its mean is about 0.386 for Poisson (integrable or localised) and 0.531 for GOE (chaotic) spectra.
A phase of strongly disordered interacting systems in which local information does not spread and the system fails to thermalise.
A regime in which a many-body system scrambles local information across all its degrees of freedom and its level statistics follow random-matrix theory.
The energy-level statistics of random matrices, with repulsion between neighbouring levels; the signature of quantum chaos.
Uncorrelated energy levels, typical of integrable and localised systems.

A channel that does not map the identity to itself, such as amplitude damping or a reset; it pulls states toward a particular state instead of toward $I/d$, which keeps reservoir features informative.
The rate at which a quantum reservoir loses information to its environment; reservoir performance is non-monotonic in it, too little giving no echo state property and too much erasing the inputs.
The factor $c<1$ by which one input step shrinks the trace distance between any two reservoir states; inputs older than about $1/\ln(1/c)$ steps are strongly attenuated.
A quantum reservoir built from bosonic modes (light, resonators, mechanical oscillators), read through quadratures or photon-number populations.
The position-like and momentum-like operators $x=(a+a^\dagger)/\sqrt2$ and $p=i(a^\dagger-a)/\sqrt2$ of a bosonic mode, with $[x,p]=i$.
A bosonic state fully described by its first moments and covariance matrix; quadratic Hamiltonians and loss keep states Gaussian, which makes them efficiently classically simulable.
The matrix $\sigma_{jk}=\tfrac12\langle\{r_j-\bar r_j,r_k-\bar r_k\}\rangle$ of second moments of the quadratures, which with the first moments fixes a Gaussian state.
Measuring a quadrature of a light or microwave mode by interfering it with a strong reference field; the standard readout of a Gaussian reservoir.
A term $K a^{\dagger2}a^2$ in an oscillator Hamiltonian that makes its frequency depend on photon number; the nonlinear element of a single-oscillator quantum reservoir.
A state $\vert n\rangle$ with exactly $n$ excitations of a bosonic mode; its populations $P_n$ serve as the features of an oscillator reservoir.
The state $\vert\alpha\rangle$ of a driven linear oscillator, with Poisson photon-number distribution $P_n=e^{-\vert\alpha\vert^2}\vert\alpha\vert^{2n}/n!$.
Keeping only the lowest $N$ number states of a mode in simulation; valid only when the top population is negligible.
A memoryless quantum reservoir: each input is encoded into a fresh state, sent through a fixed channel and measured, and only a linear readout is trained.
A one-hidden-layer neural network whose hidden weights are random and fixed, with only the linear output layer trained.
The POVM $E_k=\mathcal{E}^\dagger(\Pi_k)$ on the input obtained by absorbing a reservoir channel into the final measurement; a QELM's predictions are expectations of operators in its span.
A measurement whose effects span all operators on the system ($d^2$ of them for dimension $d$), so its outcome statistics determine the state and any expectation value.
Feeding quantum states directly into a fixed quantum reservoir and training a readout on its measurement statistics to estimate the states' properties (Ghosh et al. 2019).
Reconstructing a quantum state, or its expectation values, by a readout trained on known states measured through an informationally complete reservoir.
An entanglement measure for two qubits; for a pure state $a\vert00\rangle+b\vert01\rangle+c\vert10\rangle+d\vert11\rangle$ it is $C=2\vert ad-bc\vert$, and $C^2=2(1-\operatorname{Tr}\rho_A^2)$.
An observable $W$ with $\operatorname{Tr}[W\rho]\ge0$ for every separable state, so a negative value certifies entanglement; linear in $\rho$, hence learnable by a linear readout.
Reconstructing the density matrix of a quantum input injected into a reservoir several steps earlier from the reservoir's current observables (Tran and Nakajima 2021).
A positive semidefinite, unit-trace operator $\rho$ describing a quantum state, pure or mixed; expectation values are $\operatorname{Tr}(O\rho)$.
$\operatorname{Tr}\rho^2$: 1 for a pure state, down to $1/d$ for the maximally mixed state; for a qubit $(1+\vert\vec r\vert^2)/2$.
The map $\rho_{AB}\mapsto\rho_B = \operatorname{Tr}_A\rho_{AB}$ that gives the reduced state reproducing every local expectation on $B$.
The $4^n-1$ expectations $r_P = \operatorname{Tr}(P\rho)$ of the non-identity Pauli strings, which fix an $n$-qubit state and act as a quantum reservoir's full internal state.
A linear map on states that is completely positive and trace preserving; every physical evolution of an open system, including one input step of a quantum reservoir.
Operators $K_m$ with $\sum_m K_m^\dagger K_m = I$ that write a channel as $\rho\mapsto\sum_m K_m\rho K_m^\dagger$.
The representation of any channel as a unitary on system plus environment followed by tracing out the environment.
The matrix $\sum_{ij}\vert i\rangle\langle j\vert\otimes\mathcal{E}(\vert i\rangle\langle j\vert)$; the map $\mathcal{E}$ is completely positive iff it is positive semidefinite.
The channel of energy relaxation to $\vert0\rangle$ with probability $\gamma$; on the Bloch vector $(x,y,z)\mapsto(\sqrt{1-\gamma}x,\sqrt{1-\gamma}y,(1-\gamma)z+\gamma)$.
The channel $\rho\mapsto(1-p)\rho+pI/d$, which shrinks every Bloch vector by $1-p$.
A channel that maps the identity to itself, $\mathcal{E}(I)=I$; for a qubit, one whose Bloch map has no shift term.
The generator $\dot\rho = -i[H,\rho]+\sum_j\gamma_j(L_j\rho L_j^\dagger-\tfrac12\{L_j^\dagger L_j,\rho\})$ of a Markovian semigroup of channels.
An operator $L_j$ in a Lindblad equation describing one way the environment acts on the system, such as $\sigma^-$ for energy loss or $Z$ for dephasing.
The linear superoperator $\mathcal{L}$ generating open-system evolution $\rho(t)=e^{t\mathcal{L}}\rho(0)$, often written as a $d^2\times d^2$ matrix.
Minus the largest nonzero real part of the Liouvillian's eigenvalues: the slowest relaxation rate, whose inverse sets how long an open system remembers its past.
The time constant of a qubit's excited-state population decay, $\rho_{11}(t)=\rho_{11}(0)e^{-t/T_1}$.
The time constant of a qubit's coherence decay, with $1/T_2 = 1/(2T_1)+1/T_\varphi$ and hence $T_2\le2T_1$.
$D(\rho,\sigma)=\tfrac12\Vert\rho-\sigma\Vert_1$, the largest difference in outcome probability any measurement can see between two states.
The worst-case factor $\eta(\mathcal{E})\le1$ by which a channel shrinks the trace distance between two states; uniform $\eta<1$ over inputs gives a reservoir fading memory.

A channel with a unique, full-rank fixed state to which every initial state converges, at a rate set by its second-largest eigenvalue modulus (without the full-rank condition the channel is called mixing).
The set of operators $E_m\ge0$, $\sum_mE_m=I$, giving the outcome probabilities $p_m=\operatorname{Tr}(E_m\rho)$ of a general quantum measurement.
A causal, time-invariant map from input sequences to outputs in which inputs further in the past have less and less influence; the target class of reservoir computing.
The property that a family of reservoirs with linear (or polynomial) readouts can approximate any fading-memory filter to any accuracy, usually proved with the Stone–Weierstrass theorem.
A family of continuous functions on a compact space that contains constants, separates points and is closed under sums and products is dense in all continuous functions.
Encoding the same input more than once into a quantum model, which raises the degree (or frequency range) of the functions of that input the model can express.
The number of linearly independent readout features; for an $n$-qubit reservoir read through expectation values it is at most $4^n - 1$ per time step.
The shrinking, as $1/\sqrt{2^n}$ or faster, of how much an observable's expectation varies with the input when the dynamics scramble like a random unitary or are strongly noisy.
An ensemble of unitaries whose first and second moments match the Haar measure; enough to make Pauli expectations concentrate with variance $1/(2^n+1)$.
A pure state drawn uniformly (unitarily invariantly) from the unit sphere of a Hilbert space.
The number of feature directions whose input-driven variance exceeds the shot-noise variance, roughly $\sum_i \sigma_i^2/(\sigma_i^2 + 1/S)$; what a reservoir really offers its readout.
Simulating a channel by sampling pure-state histories with random measurement or jump outcomes, whose average reproduces the density matrix; memory $2^n$ instead of $4^n$.
A task on which a quantum reservoir reaches given accuracy with fewer resources than the best classical method, or a provable separation in what can be learned or computed.
Nearest-neighbour XX and Z spin chains map to quadratic fermion Hamiltonians, whose dynamics and single-particle observables are classically computable in polynomial time.
The operator $\prod_i Z_i$; Hamiltonians built from $X_iX_j$ and $Z_i$ conserve it, splitting the state space into even and odd sectors.
